All darkness--</hi>that is, every calamity that befalls the wicked shall be hid (in store for him) in His (God's) secret places, or treasures (Jude 13; <reference osisRef="Deut.32.34">De 32:34</reference>).<div eID="gen7182" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7183" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not blown--</hi>not kindled by man's hands, but by God's (<reference osisRef="Isa.30.33">Is 30:33</reference>; the Septuagint in the Alexandrian Manuscript reads "unquenchable fire," <reference osisRef="Matt.3.12">Mt 3:12</reference>). Tact is shown by the friends in not expressly mentioning, but alluding under color of general cases, to Job's calamities; here (<reference osisRef="Job.1.16">Job 1:16</reference>) Umbreit explains it, wickedness, is a "self-igniting fire"; in it lie the principles of destruction.<div eID="gen7183" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7184" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ill ... tabernacle--</hi>Every trace of the sinner must be obliterated (<reference osisRef="Job.18.15">Job 18:15</reference>). <div eID="gen7184" type="x-p"/>
